questions.q: The Mughal school of painting formed the spinal column of different schools of Indian miniature art. Which one of the following painting styles was not affected by Mughal painting? [1995]
questions.e: Mughal painting was aristocratic and celebrated imperial pomp and circumstances. While it influenced the Pahari, Rajasthani, and Kangra schools, the Kalighata style remained unaffected as it did not belong to the same temper or tradition.

questions.q: Who among the following were famous jurists of medieval India? 1️⃣ Vijnanesvara 2️⃣ Hemadri 3️⃣ Rajasekhara 4️⃣ Jimutavahana [1995]
questions.e: Vijnanesvara, Hemadri, and Jimutavahana were renowned jurists in medieval India. Rajasekhara, however, was a Sanskrit poet and dramatist, not a jurist.

questions.q: Which one of the following monuments has a dome which is said to be one of the largest in the world? [1995]
questions.e: The Gol Gumbaz in Bijapur is the mausoleum of Muhammad Adil Shah. It features a dome that is recognized as the second largest in the world.

questions.q: Ashtapradhan was a council of ministers: [1995]
questions.e: The Ashtapradhan was a formal council of eight ministers established by Shivaji to assist in the Maratha administration.

questions.q: The route indicated in the map was followed, during the course of his military exploits, by: [1995]
questions.e: The map indicates the southern expedition route taken by Malik Kafur, also known as Hazar Dinari. He was sent by Alauddin Khalji and reached as far as Kanyakumari.

questions.q: The term 'Apabhramsa' was used in medieval Sanskrit texts to denote: [1996]
o: early forms of some of the modern Indian language
questions.e: Before the rise of modern Indian languages, Apabhramsa was the most vibrant language used for colloquial and literary works in North India.

questions.q: Nastaliq was: [1996]
o: a cess levied by the Mughal rulers
a persian script used in medieval India
a manual of code of conduct for the Ulemas
questions.e: Nastaliq was a popular Persian script used for writing and calligraphy during the Mughal period in medieval India.

questions.q: The sufi saint who maintained that devotional music was one way of coming close to God was: [1996]
questions.e: Shaikh Muin-ud-din Chishti introduced the Chishti Silsilah in India. He emphasized "Wahd-tul-wajud" and used Sama (devotional music) and Mehfil as means to get closer to God.

questions.q: Mughal painting reached its zenith under: [1996]
questions.e: Mughal painting reached its highest point of development and artistic excellence during the reign of Emperor Jahangir (1605–1627).

questions.q: In medieval India, Mansabdari system was introduced for: [1996]
questions.e: The Mansabdari system, introduced by Akbar around 1595-96, was a unique administrative system that showed a noble's civil and military capacity to ensure efficient governance.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched? [1996]
questions.e: Guru Arjun Dev is credited with the compilation of the Adi Granth. The concepts of Miri and Piri were introduced by Guru Hargobind, and the Dal Khalsa was associated with Guru Gobind Singh's legacy.

questions.q: Prem Vatika, poems on the life of Krishna, were composed by: [1996]
questions.e: Raskhan (c. 1558–1628) was a Muslim poet and a devoted follower of Lord Krishna who composed the "Prem Vatika."

questions.q: After consolidating his power, Balban assumed the grand title of: [1997]
questions.e: Ghiyas-ud-din Balban was influenced by Persian court models and assumed the title "Zil-i-Ilahi," which means "Shadow of God."

questions.q: Head of the military department under the recognised central machinery of administration during Akbar's reign was: [1997]
questions.e: The Mir Bakshi was the head of the military and intelligence department under Akbar. He served as the paymaster-general and managed intelligence officers and news reporters.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The sponsor and the most prominent figure of the Chisti order of Sufis in India is Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti Reason (R): The Chisti order takes its name from a village Chisti in Ajmer. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct? [1997]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: While Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti is the prominent figure of the order in India, the order actually takes its name from Chisht, a small town near Herat in Afghanistan, not Ajmer.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of composers in different languages and their works on the Mahabharata theme is correctly matched? [1997]
questions.e: Pampa was a famous Kannada poet whose work "Vikramarjuna Vijaya" (also known as Pampa Bharata) is a Kannada version of the Mahabharata.

questions.q: The medieval Indian writer who refers to the discovery of America is: [1997]
questions.e: Abul Fazl, the author of Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari, is the medieval writer who makes a reference to the discovery of America.

questions.q: The member of Shivaji's Ashtapradhan who looked after foreign affairs was: [1998]
questions.e: In Shivaji’s council of ministers (Ashtapradhan), the Sumant was the minister in charge of foreign affairs.

questions.q: The loss of Qandhar was a big blow to the Mughal empire from the view point of: [1998]
questions.e: Qandhar was a vital strategic stronghold. Although recovered by Shah Jahan in 1638, its final loss to the Iranians in 1649 was a major setback for Mughal defense.

questions.q: Fawazil in the Sultanate period meant: [1998]
o: revenue assigned in lieu of salary
excess amount paid to the exchequer by the Iqtadars
illegal exactions extracted from the peasants
questions.e: During the Sultanate period, Fawazil referred to the surplus amount that Iqtadars (land-grant holders) were required to pay to the central government after meeting their expenses.

questions.q: Sultan of Delhi who is reputed to have built the biggest network of canals in India was: [1998]
questions.e: Firoz Shah Tughlaq is famous for building and repairing a vast network of canals to improve agriculture in India.

questions.q: Assertion (A): At first the Turkish administration in India was essentially military. Reason (R): The country was parcelled out as 'Iqtas' among leading military leaders. [1998]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: The initial Turkish rule was military-based because the Sultans distributed land as 'Iqtas' to military chiefs to maintain troops, which they could take back if requirements weren't met.

questions.q: Assertion (A): During the reign of Shahjahan, Dara Sikoh was sent on expedition to Balkha, Badakhshan and Qandahar. Reason (R): The expedition sent by Shahjahan to the Middle-East was a marvellous success. [1998]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: While Shahjahan did send expeditions to central Asia, including Balkh and Badakhshan, these campaigns were actually military failures and did not achieve success.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: Ahadis were those troopers who: 1️⃣ offered their services singly 2️⃣ did not attach themselves to any chief 3️⃣ had the emperor as their immediate colonel 4️⃣ attached themselves to Mirzas. Of these statements: [1998]
questions.e: Ahadis were elite "gentlemen troopers" recruited individually. They were loyal only to the emperor and had their own diwan and bakshi rather than serving under common chiefs.

questions.q: Consider the following: 1️⃣ Tughlaqabad fort 2️⃣ Lodi Garden 3️⃣ Qutab Minar 4️⃣ Fatehpur Sikri. The correct chronological order in which they were built is: [1998]
questions.e: Qutab Minar (1206-36), Tughlaqabad Fort (1321), Lodi Garden (1451-1526), and Fatehpur Sikri (built by Akbar starting in 1570).

questions.q: Match List-I (Events) with List-II (Dates): A. Battle of Haldi Ghati (1) 1556, B. Grant of Charter to EIC (2) 1600, C. Accession of Akbar (3) 1686, D. Death of Shivaji (4) 1739, E. Nadir Shah's capture of Delhi (5) 1576. Select the correct code: [1998]
questions.e: Accession of Akbar was in 1556, Battle of Haldighati in 1576, Charter to East India Company in 1600, Death of Shivaji in 1680, and Nadir Shah's invasion in 1739.

questions.q: In the given map, the shaded part represents Akbar's empire at a certain juncture, A stands for an independent country and 'B' marks the site of city. Which one of the following alternative gives all correct information? [1998]
questions.e: The map shows Akbar's empire at the time of his death in 1605. At this point, Gondwana (A) was represented and Lahore (B) was a key city.

questions.q: The first writer to use Urdu as the medium of poetic expression was: [1999]
questions.e: Amir Khusrau (1253–1325), though a Persian poet, was the first to use Urdu (Hindavi) as a medium for poetic expression.

questions.q: To which Lodi Sultan does the given map relate and what town does the site marked A represent? [1999]
questions.e: Bahlol Lodi defeated Hussain Shah Sharqi and annexed Jaunpur (marked A) in 1479.

questions.q: Assertion (A): During the time of Akbar, for every ten cavalrymen, the mansabdars had to maintain twenty horses. Reason (R): Horses had to be rested while on march and replacements were necessary in times of war. [1999]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: The "Du-aspa Sih-aspa" (two-horse three-horse) system was actually introduced by Jahangir, not Akbar. Therefore, Assertion A is incorrect.

questions.q: One consistent feature found in the history of southern India was the growth of small regional kingdoms rather than large empires because of: [1999]
o: absence of vast areas of fertile land
too many divisions in the social structure
questions.e: The lack of vast, continuous stretches of fertile land in southern India (unlike the Indo-Gangetic plains) limited the ability of rulers to sustain large, centralized empires.

questions.q: 'The king was freed from his people and they from their king'. On whose death did Badauni comment thus? [1999]
questions.e: This famous remark was made by the historian Badauni upon the death of Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq in 1351, whose unconventional policies had caused much friction.

questions.q: The striking feature of the Jama Masjid in Kashmir completed by Zain-ul-Abdin include(s): 1️⃣ turret 2️⃣ similarity with Buddhist pagodas 3️⃣ Persian style. Which of the above statements is/are correct? [1999]
questions.e: The Jama Masjid in Srinagar, extended by Zain-ul-Abdin, is unique for its architecture which shows similarities to Buddhist pagodas and incorporates Persian styles.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [1999]
questions.e: Sir Thomas Roe was the ambassador of King James I and visited the court of Jahangir, not Akbar.

questions.q: Match List-I (Land Systems) with List-II (Definitions): A. Jagirdari, B. Ryotwari, C. Mahalwari, D. Zamindari. [2000]
questions.e: In Jagirdari, land is given to big feudal lords; Ryotwari involves direct settlement with peasants; Mahalwari is settlement at the village level; Zamindari involves revenue farmers/rent collectors.

questions.q: Who among the following streamlined the Maratha administration after Sambhaji? [2000]
questions.e: Balaji Vishwanath played a crucial role in consolidating the Maratha administration and securing victory for Shahu by winning over various Maratha sardars.

questions.q: The given map refers to the kingdom of: [2000]
o: Aurangzeb at the time of his death in 1707
Akbar at the time of capture of Khandesh in 1601
Akbar at the time of his death in 1605
Aurangzeb at the time of capture of Hyderabad
questions.e: The shaded portion on the map represents the territory of Khandesh, which Akbar annexed in 1601.

questions.q: Consider the following events: 1️⃣ Reign of Krishna Deva of Vijaynagara 2️⃣ Construction of Qutab Minar 3️⃣ Arrival of Portuguese in India 4️⃣ Death of Firoz Tughlaq. Correct chronological sequence is: [2000]
questions.e: Construction of Qutab Minar (1206), Death of Firoz Tughlaq (1388), Arrival of Portuguese (1498), and Reign of Krishna Deva (1509–30).

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II: A. Iqta (1) Marathas, B. Jagir (2) Delhi Sultans, C. Amaram (3) Mughals, D. Mokasa (4) Vijayanagara. [2000]
questions.e: Iqta was used by Delhi Sultans, Jagir by Mughals, Amaram by Vijayanagara, and Mokasa by the Marathas.

questions.q: Which one of the following Muslim rulers was hailed as the 'Jagadguru' by his Muslim subject because of his belief in secularism? [2000]
questions.e: Ibrahim Adil Shah II (1556–1627) of Bijapur was known for his secular outlook and was called "Jagadguru" by his subjects.

questions.q: In which one of the following cities is the Lingaraja Temple located? [2001]
questions.e: The Lingaraja Temple was built by Yayati Kesari and is located in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

questions.q: Match Bhakti Saint (List-I) with Profession (List-II): A. Namdev (1) Barber, B. Kabir (2) Weaver, C. Ravidas (3) Tailor, D. Sena (4) Cobbler. [2001]
questions.e: The professions of these Bhakti saints were: Namdev was a tailor, Kabir was a weaver, Ravidas was a cobbler, and Sena was a barber.

questions.q: Mongols under Chengiz Khan invaded India during the reign of: [2001]
questions.e: Chengiz Khan reached the Indian frontier during Iltutmish's reign while pursuing the Persian king, but Iltutmish avoided a direct invasion by refusing the king shelter.

questions.q: Which among the following ports was called Babul Makka (Gate of Makka) during the Mughal period? [2001]
questions.e: Surat was known as the "Gate of Makka" because it was the primary port from which pilgrims departed for the Hajj pilgrimage.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched? [2001]
questions.e: Dewan-i-Bandagani (Department of Slaves) was created by Firoz Shah Tughlaq. Dewan-i-Mustakhraj was by Alauddin Khalji, Dewan-i-Kohi by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq, and Dewan-i-Arz by Balban.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Battle of Khanua was certainly more decisive and significant than the First Battle of Panipat. Reason (R): Rana Sanga, the Rajput hero, was certainly a more formidable adversary than Ibrahim Lodi. [2001]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Rana Sanga had previously defeated Ibrahim Lodi and led a powerful confederacy; defeating him at Khanua (1527) was more critical for Babur than his victory at Panipat (1526).

questions.q: The shaded area in the above map shows the empire of: [2000]
questions.e: The map illustrates the extent of the Mughal Empire under Shahjahan, who expanded into Rajput kingdoms and the Deccan (Bijapur and Golconda).

questions.q: Who among the following was the first Bhakti saint to use Hindi for the propagation of his message? [2002]
questions.e: Ramananda (1360–1470) was the first major Bhakti saint to use the local language (Hindi) instead of Sanskrit to reach the common people.

questions.q: With reference to medieval Indian rulers, which one of the following statement is correct? [2002]
o: Balban introduced the branding of horses in his military.
Firoz Tughlaq set up a separate department of slaves.
Muhammad Bin Tughlaq was succeeded by his uncle.
Alauddin Khalji first set up a separate ariz's department.
questions.e: Firoz Shah Tughlaq created a dedicated department for slaves called 'Diwan-i-Bandagan'. Balban was the one who set up the Ariz's department, and Alauddin Khalji introduced horse branding.

questions.q: The motive behind Shah Jahan's Balkh campaign was to: [2002]
o: secure a friendly ruler in Balkh and Badakshan which bordered Kabul
conquer Samarqand and Farghana, the Mughal homelands
fix the Mughal frontier on the 'scientific line', the Amu Daria
expand the Mughal Empire beyond the sub-continent
questions.e: Shah Jahan's campaign in Central Asia was aimed at establishing a friendly buffer state to secure the defense of the North-West frontier.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Muhammad Bin Tughlaq left Delhi, and for two years lived in a camp called Swarga-Dwari. Reason (R): At that time, Delhi was ravaged by plague and many people died. [2002]
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true but R is not a correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq stayed in a camp called Swargadwari near Kanauj for two years because Delhi was suffering from a severe famine and plague.

questions.q: Historian Barani refused to consider the state in India under Delhi Sultans as truly Islamic because: [2002]
o: Sultan supplemented the Muslim law by framing his own regulations
majority of the population did not follow Islam
religious freedom was accorded to non-muslims
questions.e: Barani felt the state was not truly Islamic because Sultans often prioritized state laws (Zawabit) over traditional Islamic law (Sharia) to manage the vast non-Muslim population.

questions.q: With reference to Sufism in Indian history, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Sheikh Ahmad Sarhandi was a contemporary of Ibrahim Lodi 2️⃣ Sheikh Nasiruddin Chirag-I-Dehlavi was a disciple of Sheikh Nizamuddin Auliya 3️⃣ Aurangzeb was a contemporary of Sheikh Salim Chisti 4️⃣ Qadiri order of Sufis was first introduced in India by Sheikh Niamutullah and Makhdum Muhammad Jilani. Which of these statements are correct? [2002]
questions.e: Sheikh Ahmad Sarhandi was a contemporary of Akbar and Jahangir, not Lodi. Sheikh Salim Chisti was a contemporary of Akbar. Statements 2 and 4 are historically accurate.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Emperor Akbar marched towards Afghanistan in 1581 with a huge army. Reason (R): He was on his way to reclaim his ancestral country of Ferghana in Central Asia. [2003]
o: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.e: Akbar marched to Kabul in 1581 to expand his kingdom and suppress revolt, but he had no intention or plan to reclaim Ferghana.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Shah Alam II spent the initial years as an emperor far away from his capital. Reason (R): There was always a lurking danger of foreign invasion from the north-west frontier. [2003]
o: Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Shah Alam II stayed away from Delhi due to the dominance and fear of Najib Khan Rohilla within the capital, not primarily due to foreign invasions.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Saluva Narasimha put an end to the old dynasty and assumed the royal title. Reason (R): He wanted to save the kingdom from further degeneration and disintegration. [2003]
o: Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Saluva Narasimha ended the Sangama dynasty and started the Saluva dynasty to prevent the Vijayanagara Empire from collapsing due to weak internal rule.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Marathas emerged as the strongest native power in India after the decline of Mughal empire. Reason (R): Marathas were the first to have a clear concept of a united Indian nation. [2003]
o: Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are individually true but R is the correct explanation of A
questions.e: While the Marathas were the most powerful native force after the Mughals, they did not possess a modern concept of a "united Indian nation."

questions.q: Alam Khan, one of those who invited Babur to invade India was: [2003]
o: a high official in Punjab province who was discontented with Ibrahim Lodi's treatment to his tribe
the father of Dilawar Khan to whom cruel treatment was meted out by Ibrahim Lodi
an uncle of Ibrahim Lodi and a pretender to the throne of Delhi
a cousin of Ibrahim Lodi who was ill-treated and expelled from the country
questions.e: Alam Khan was the uncle of the Sultan Ibrahim Lodi and sought Babur's help to displace his nephew and take the throne.

questions.q: Battle of Dharmat was fought between: [2003]
o: Ahmad Shah Durrani and the Marathas
questions.e: The Battle of Dharmat (1658) was a crucial conflict in the Mughal war of succession where Aurangzeb defeated the forces of his brother Dara Shikoh.

questions.q: How did the Mughal Emperor Jahandarshah's reign, come to an early end? [2003]
o: He died of sickness due to drinking
He died due to a slip while climbing down the steps
He was deposed by his Wazir
He was defeated by his nephew in a battle
questions.e: Jahandarshah was defeated in battle by his nephew Farrukh Siyyar, who was aided by the powerful Sayyid Brothers.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Kitab-i-Nauras, a collection of songs in praise of Hindu deities and Muslim saints, was written by Ibrahim Adil Shah II 2️⃣ Amir Khusrau was the originator in India of the early form of the musical style known as Qawali. Which of these statements is/are correct? [2003]
questions.e: Ibrahim Adil Shah II wrote the "Kitab-i-Nauras," and Amir Khusrau is recognized as the "Father of Qawali" in India.

questions.q: How did Sultan Qutb-ud-din Aibak die? [2003]
o: He was treacherously stabbed to death by one of his ambitious nobles
He sustained injuries while besieging the fortress of Kalinjar
He died after a fall from his horse while playing Chaugan
He was killed in a battle with Taj-u-din Yildiz
questions.e: Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the founder of the Slave Dynasty, died in 1210 following a fall from his horse while playing Chaugan (polo).

questions.q: Which one of the following sequences indicates the correct chronological order? [2004]
questions.e: The correct timeline is: Shankaracharya (9th Century), Ramanuja (1017–1137), and Chaitanya (1486–1533).

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Narasimha Saluva ended the Sangama dynasty and seized the throne for himself and started the Saluva dynasty. 2️⃣ Vira Narasimha deposed the last Saluva ruler and seized the throne for himself. 3️⃣ Vira Narasimha was succeeded by his younger brother, Krishnadeva Raya. 4️⃣ Krishnadeva Raya was succeeded by his half brother, Achyuta Raya. Which of the statements given above are correct? [2004]
questions.e: All these statements correctly describe the transitions of power in the Vijayanagara Empire from the Sangama to Saluva and Taluva dynasties.

questions.q: Who was the last ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate? [2004]
questions.e: Nasiruddin Mahmud (1395–1412) was the final ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.

questions.q: How did the dynasty of Nizam Shahis of Ahmadnagar come to an end? [2004]
o: Malik Ambar was defeated in a battle with Mughals in 1631
Mughal troops destroyed Daulatabad fort and killed Nizam-ul Mulk of Ahmadnagar
Ahmadnagar was annexed into Mughal empire and Hussain Shah was given life imprisonment
Fateh Khan usurped the throne from Nizam-ul-Mulk
questions.e: Ahmadnagar was annexed by Shahjahan in 1633, and the last ruler, Hussain Shah, was sent to life imprisonment in Gwalior.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about Sikh Gurus: 1️⃣ Banda Bahadur was appointed as the military leader of the Sikhs by Guru Tegh Bahadur. 2️⃣ Guru Arjun Dev became the Sikh Guru after Guru Ram Das. 3️⃣ Guru Arjun Dev gave to Sikhs their own script Guru Mukhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2004]
questions.e: Guru Arjun Dev was the son and successor of Guru Ram Das. Banda Bahadur was appointed by Guru Gobind Singh, and the Gurmukhi script was popularized by Guru Angad.

questions.q: The initial design and construction of which massive temple took place during the reign of Suryavarman II? [2006]
questions.e: Angkor Vat, originally dedicated to Vishnu and now the world's largest religious structure, was built during the reign of King Suryavarman II.

questions.q: When Raja Wodeyar founded the kingdom of Mysore, who was the ruler of the Vijayanagar Empire? [2006]
questions.e: The Wodeyar dynasty established its rule in Mysore while Venkata II was reigning over the declining Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.q: In the year 1613, where was the English East India Company given permission to set up a factory (trading post)? [2006]
questions.e: In 1613, the Mughals gave the English East India Company permission to establish their first permanent trading post or factory at Surat.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Muhammad bin Tughlaq issued a new gold coin which was called Dinar by Ibn Batutah. Reason (R): Muhammad bin Tughlaq wanted to issue token currency in gold coins to promote trade with West Asian and North African countries. [2006]
o: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A are Rare true but R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
questions.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq did issue a gold coin called Dinar, but his famous "token currency" experiment involved bronze and copper coins, not gold.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the Afghan rulers to the throne of Delhi? [2006]
questions.e: The Lodi dynasty rulers were Bahlol Lodi (1451–1489), followed by Sikandar Lodi (1489–1517), and finally Ibrahim Lodi (1517–1526).

questions.q: Bhakta Tukaram was a contemporary of which Mughal emperor? [2006]
questions.e: Bhakta Tukaram (1608–1650) lived during the period when Jahangir (reigned 1605–1627) was the Mughal emperor.

questions.q: In Indian history, who was Abdul Hamid Lahori? [2006]
o: A chronicler and poet during the reign of Muhammad Shah.
An important noble and confidant of Aurangzeb.
An important military commander during Akbar reign.
An official historian of the reign of Shahjahan.
questions.e: Abdul Hamid Lahori was the court historian for Emperor Shahjahan and wrote the "Padshah Nama," which documents Shahjahan's reign.

questions.q: Where is the famous Vijaya Vittala temple having its 56 carved pillars emitting musical notes located? [2007]
questions.e: The Vijaya Vittala temple, famous for its musical pillars and stone chariot, is located in Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.q: During the time of which Mughal Emperor did the English East India Company establish its first factory in India? [2008]
questions.e: Although the Company formed during Akbar's reign, they established their first factory at Surat in 1613 under the reign of Jahangir.

questions.q: Where is the famous Virupaksha temple located? [2009]
questions.e: The Virupaksha temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva, is located in Hampi on the banks of the Tungabhadra River and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.q: Match List-I (Famous Temple) with List-II (State): A. Vidyashankara temple (1) Andhra Pradesh, B. Rajarani temple (2) Karnataka, C. Kandariya Mahadeo (3) Madhya Pradesh, D. Bhimesvara temple (4) Orissa. [2009]
questions.e: Vidyashankara is in Karnataka, Rajarani is in Orissa, Kandariya Mahadeo is in Madhya Pradesh, and Bhimesvara is in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: With whose permission did the English set up their first factory in Surat? [2009]
questions.e: The English East India Company established its first factory in Surat in 1613 after receiving a farman (royal decree) from Emperor Jahangir.

questions.q: Among the following, who was not a proponent of Bhakti cult? [2010]
questions.e: Tukaram, Tyagaraja, and Vallabhacharya were all key figures in the Bhakti movement. Nagarjuna, however, was an early Buddhist philosopher and founder of Madhyamika philosophy.

questions.q: Why did Buddhism start declining in India in the early medieval times? 1️⃣ Buddha was by that time considered as one of the incarnations of Vishnu and thus became a part of Vaishnavism. 2️⃣ Invading tribes from Central Asia till the time of last Gupta king adopted Hinduism and persecuted Buddhists. 3️⃣ Kings of Gupta dynasty were strongly opposed to Buddhism. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2010]
questions.e: Buddhism declined as it was absorbed into Hinduism (Buddha as Vishnu's 9th incarnation). Central Asian tribes didn't specifically persecute Buddhists, and the Guptas, while Hindu, did not actively oppose Buddhism.

questions.q: With reference to Dhrupad, one of the major traditions of India that has been kept alive for centuries, which of the following statements are correct? 1️⃣ Dhrupad originated and developed in the Rajput kingdoms during the Mughal period. 2️⃣ Dhrupad is primarily a devotional and spiritual music. 3️⃣ Dhrupad Alap uses Sanskrit syllables from Mantras. [2012-1]
o: None of the above is correct
questions.e: Dhrupad is a spiritual and devotional tradition that uses Sanskrit syllables from mantras in its Alap. It did not originate solely in Rajput kingdoms during the Mughal period.

questions.q: With reference to the religious history of medieval India, the Sufi mystics were known to pursue which of the following practices? 1️⃣ Meditation and control of breath 2️⃣ Severe ascetic exercises in a lonely place 3️⃣ Recitation of holy songs to arouse a state of ecstasy in their audience. [2012-1]
questions.e: Sufi mystics employed various spiritual practices, including breath control, extreme asceticism, and the recitation of holy songs (Sama) to achieve mystical states.

questions.q: Consider the following Bhakti Saints: 1️⃣ Dadu Dayal 2️⃣ Guru Nanak 3️⃣ Tyagaraja. Who among the above was/were preaching when the Lodi dynasty fell and Babur took over? [2013-1]
questions.e: Guru Nanak (1469–1539) was traveling and preaching when Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in 1526. Dadu Dayal and Tyagaraja lived in later centuries.

questions.q: Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri was: [2014-1]
o: the room in which the nobles belonging to different religions gathered to discuss religious affairs
the hall in which Akbar held discussions with scholars of various religions
the mosque for the use of Royal Family
questions.e: Built by Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri, the Ibadat Khana was a meeting house where he invited scholars of different faiths to discuss and debate religious matters.

questions.q: In medieval India, the designations 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' were used for: [2014-1]
questions.e: In the administrative structure of medieval India, 'Mahattara' and 'Pattakila' were terms specifically used to denote village headmen.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs (State-Region): 1️⃣ Champaka-Central India 2️⃣ Durgara-Jammu 3️⃣ Kuluta-Malabar. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched? [2015-1]
questions.e: Durgara corresponds to the Jammu region. Champaka is Chamba and Kuluta is Kulu (both in the Himalayan region), not Central India or Malabar.

questions.q: The arrival of Babur into India led to the: 1️⃣ introduction of gunpowder in the subcontinent 2️⃣ introduction of the arch and dome in the region's architecture 3️⃣ establishment of Timurid dynasty in the region. [2015-1]
questions.e: Gunpowder was known in India before Babur, and the Delhi Sultanate had already introduced the arch and dome. Babur's arrival specifically established the Timurid (Mughal) dynasty.

questions.q: Who of the following founded a new city on the south bank of a tributary to river Krishna and undertook to rule his new kingdom as the agent of a deity? [2015-1]
questions.e: Harihara I and Bukka founded the city of Vijayanagara in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra (a tributary of the Krishna) and ruled as representatives of the deity Virupaksha.

questions.q: Banjaras during the medieval period of Indian history were generally: [2016-1]
questions.e: Banjaras were traditional trader-nomads who moved goods like salt, grain, and cattle across the country.

questions.q: Who of the following had first deciphered the edicts of Emperor Ashoka? [2016-1]
questions.e: James Prinsep, a British archaeologist and official, deciphered the Ashokan edicts in 1837, identifying the king as "Piyadasi."

questions.q: With reference to the religious history of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The concept of Bodhisattva is central to Hinayana sect of Buddhism. 2️⃣ Bodhisattva is a compassionate one on his way to enlightenment. 3️⃣ Bodhisattva delays achieving his own salvation to help all sentient beings on their path to it. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2016-1]
questions.e: The concept of Bodhisattva is central to the Mahayana sect, not Hinayana. A Bodhisattva is a compassionate being striving for enlightenment while helping others.

questions.q: What is/are common to the two historical places known as Ajanta and Mahabalipuram? 1️⃣ Both were built in the same period. 2️⃣ Both belong to the same religious denomination. 3️⃣ Both have rock-cut monuments. [2016-1]
o: None of the statements given above is correct
questions.e: Both sites feature rock-cut architecture. However, Ajanta (Buddhist) was built from the 2nd Century BCE to 5th Century CE, while Mahabalipuram (Hindu) was built in the 7th-8th Centuries.

questions.q: With reference to the economic history of medieval India, the term 'Araghatta' refers to: [2016-1]
o: waterwheel used in the irrigation of land
land grants made to military officers
questions.e: 'Araghatta' (from 'ara' meaning spoke and 'ghatta' meaning pot) refers to the Persian waterwheel used for lifting water from wells for irrigation.

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of India, the memorizing of chronicles, dynastic histories and Epic tales was the profession of who of the following? [2016-1]
questions.e: The Maagadhas and Sutas were professionals responsible for preserving and reciting dynastic genealogies and epic stories.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs (Place-Region): 1️⃣ Bodhgaya-Baghelkhand 2️⃣ Khajuraho-Bundelkhand 3️⃣ Shirdi-Vidarbha 4️⃣ Nasik-Malwa 5️⃣ Tirupati-Rayalaseema. Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched? [2016-1]
questions.e: Khajuraho is in Bundelkhand and Tirupati is in Rayalaseema. Bodhgaya is in Bihar, Shirdi is in Ahmednagar, and Nasik is in the Deccan region, not Malwa.

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of medieval India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Siddhas (Sittars) of Tamil region were monotheistic and condemned idolatry. 2️⃣ Lingayats of Kannada region questioned the theory of rebirth and rejected the caste hierarchy. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2016-1]
questions.e: Both groups were reformist; the Siddhas were monotheists who rejected idols, and the Lingayats famously rejected caste and the traditional doctrine of rebirth.

questions.q: Regarding the taxation system of Krishna Deva, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The tax rate on land was fixed depending on the quality of the land. 2️⃣ Private owners of workshops paid an industries tax. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2016-1]
questions.e: Under Krishna Deva Raya, land was classified by type to determine tax, and other levies like industry taxes on workshops were also collected.

questions.q: With reference to the cultural history of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ White marble was used in making Buland Darwaza and Khankah at Fatehpur Sikri. 2️⃣ Red sandstone and marble were used in making Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza at Lucknow. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2018-1]
questions.e: While Buland Darwaza uses red/yellow sandstone with marble inlay, the official UPSC key indicates 'd' as correct, as the Lucknow monuments were primarily built with brick and plaster.

questions.q: The well-known painting "Bani Thani" belongs to the: [2018-1]
questions.e: "Bani Thani" is a famous painting of the Kishangarh school, representing a woman believed to be the poet-king Sawant Singh's beloved.

questions.q: With reference to Mughal India, what is/are the difference/differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar? 1️⃣ Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties, whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection. 2️⃣ Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary. [2019-1]
questions.e: Both statements are incorrect. Zamindars were hereditary owners with local administration/military duties, while Jagirdars held non-hereditary revenue assignments in lieu of state service.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate, the in-charge of revenue collection was known as 'Amil'. 2️⃣ The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution. 3️⃣ The office of 'Mir Bakshi' came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2019-1]
questions.e: Only the first statement is correct. The Iqta system was not indigenous (it started with the Turks in 1206), and the Mir Bakshi was a Mughal official, not Khalji.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Saint Nimbarka was a contemporary of Akbar. 2️⃣ Saint Kabir was greatly influenced by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2019-1]
questions.e: Nimbarka lived in the 13th century, long before Akbar. Kabir (15th c.) died before Sirhindi (16th-17th c.) was born; moreover, their ideologies were radically different.

questions.q: With reference to Mian Tansen, which one of the following statement is not correct? [2019-1]
o: Tansen was the title given to him by Emperor Akbar.
Tansen composed Dhrupads on Hindu god and goddesses.
Tansen composed songs on his patrons.
questions.e: The title "Tansen" was actually given to him by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior, not by Emperor Akbar.

questions.q: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait? [2019-1]
questions.e: While painting was confined to manuscripts under Akbar, Jahangir shifted the focus toward individual portraits and organized albums (muraqqas).

questions.q: With reference to the history of India, consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Aurang: In-charge of treasury of the State 2️⃣ Banian: Indian agent of the East India Company 3️⃣ Mirasidar: Designated revenue payer to the State. Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched? [2020-1]
questions.e: Aurang is a Persian term for a warehouse, not a treasury official. Banians were agents for the EIC, and Mirasidars were designated revenue payers.
